article: How to use GNU nano on Windows with WSL or MSYS2
findings: Removed the obsolete SourceForge single-binary download and manual PATH directions; documented WSL and MSYS2 as distinct maintained environments, including their Windows support prerequisites and official setup/package references.

Corrected the categorical claim that Japanese input is unsupported. GNU nano supports internationalization and UTF-8; actual input/display depends on terminal, font, locale, and input-method configuration.
Explained MSYS2 update/restart steps and that its nano package should be run in the MSYS2 terminal, not assumed to be a native Command Prompt or PowerShell executable.

Documented reliable Ctrl+O/Enter save and Ctrl+X exit controls, with current Ctrl+S behavior linked to the official nano cheat sheet; retained the original 2024-03-31 publication date, removed the duplicate date, and added lastmod/localized descriptions.
Compared the complete Japanese article with all twelve translations, including metadata, platform prerequisites, commands and paths, shortcuts, UTF-8/input caveats, and official references.
